look_here_first: Look for a VERY LOW rhizomatous muhly: numerous extremely fine, inward-rolled threadlike leaves, slender usually 20–40 cm culms and a short narrow flowering head, sometimes partly held inside the top leaf sheath. True creeping SCALY underground rhizomes distinguish it from surface-stolon nimblewill, but rhizomes must be exposed for confirmation.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass specimen appendix documents Muhlenbergia utilis from Bandera, Blanco, Gillespie, Kerr, Llano, and Travis counties, all inside the project target zone.

best_field_traits: very narrow filiform involute leaf blades
small narrow panicle, sometimes partly included in upper sheath
often in moist depressions, stream margins, or seep-like grassland microsites
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Unlike the large bunch-forming M. lindheimeri or M. ×involuta, M. utilis is a much shorter rhizomatous grass with threadlike leaves and a small narrow inflorescence.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole low patch from the side with flowering culms in context.
Gently exposed underground scaly rhizome with leaves/stems attached and mm ruler; backfill after photograph.
Fresh rolled threadlike leaf blade cross-section + a very short membranous ligule.
Entire small inflorescence showing whether partly enclosed by the upper leaf sheath.
crew_field_check: Spot the very fine grass foliage and low growth in the original whole-patch photograph; do not mistake dry dead leaves for evidence of rhizomes.
In the closer image, trace true slender grass blades with the fingers for scale. The tiny leaf width can be seen, but their inward-rolled edges cannot be measured here.
Confirm with an exposed SCALY UNDERGROUND rhizome and ligule; distinguish nimblewill's visible surface runners from true below-ground rhizomes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: M. schreberi spreads by ABOVE-GROUND slender stolons which root at nodes, usually with short flattened leaf blades; M. utilis has underground scaly rhizomes and very fine involute blades. M. reverchonii forms a tight compact upright tuft with an open flowering panicle. Sporobolus may look similar but its spikelet structures differ on mature dissection.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Aparejo grass / Aparejo muhly — look here first
steps: PHOTO 1 — WIDE fine grassy patch beside paving. Surface mat habit only, no buried stem demonstrated.
PHOTO 2 — actual hand-level threadlike green leaves and stems. Informal finger scale cannot resolve short ligule or blade cross-section.
PHOTO 3 — source-labelled Uvalde County creeping patch below limestone. Roots and rhizome NOT excavated.
PHOTO 4 — Burnet County thin upright green shoots and narrow leaves among plant litter; rooted-in-place context, buried base hidden.
PHOTO 5 — Uvalde County fine foliage over a hand. Do not treat overlapping stems as one proven connected plant.

PHOTO 6 — actual exact-source CC0 leaf/sheath photograph (#410577695). Pale tissue is visible beside a green ribbed blade. Actual FREE ligule edge is not unambiguously certified or millimeter-measured; gently open sheath of the same fresh plant.
PHOTO 7 — actual exact-source CC0 narrow attached flowering head (#410577679) with multiple whole spikelets along its rachis. Individual glumes and lemmas are not dissected or measured in pixels.

PHOTO 8 — DIFFERENT SPECIES nimblewill (M. schreberi), showing slender leafy aboveground shoots. Confirm actual stolon ROOTING at a node versus APAREJO's underground SCALY rhizome only after digging carefully.

TO FINISH — photograph an uninterrupted living M. utilis plant showing the underground rhizome with scales, nodes, roots and connected leafy culms, beside a 1-mm ruler; and a true inner ligule measured on same plant.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use low fine-grass habit, actual narrow spikelet-bearing panicle, and narrow leaves to suspect aparejo; distinguish it from nimblewill by a positively seen scaly UNDERGROUND rhizome and true inner membranous ligule, not by inference from turf texture.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — TRACE THE LOW PATCH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Low, very fine-leaved perennial; do not mistake a surface mat for proven rhizomes.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Source-labelled Uvalde and Burnet field photographs show threadlike foliage and low patches. The 2023 Muhlenbergia revision reports upright culms about 7–30 cm, with older trailing stems sometimes reaching 1 m; earlier crew notes give 20–40 cm. Growth varies. Trace one flowering stem into the ground, but do not assert underground connections from overlapping shoots.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL FIELD HABIT — CONNECTED ROOTED BASE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · EXPOSE THE UNDERGROUND GROWTH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Confirm slender, SCALY rhizomes below soil; nimblewill instead roots at surface nodes.
field_id_short_tiles.details: M. utilis is a rhizomatous perennial. Carefully expose a single continuous underground stem with attached scales, nodes, roots and aboveground shoot where collection is permitted; replace disturbed soil. The archived grass-patch images show neither underground scales nor connected root system. A reclining shoot is not itself proof of a rhizome.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR AND ROLLED BLADE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Very narrow, often inward-rolled blades; true membranous ligule 0.2–0.8 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The 2023 revision describes blades about 0.2–1.8 mm wide and a short truncate, decurrent membranous ligule 0.2–0.8 mm long. The CC0 close-up shows a pale sheath-junction region, NOT a measured free ligule. Photograph the attached blade–sheath junction front-on and in profile at 10–20× beside a 1-mm scale; a fresh blade cross-section should show truly involute margins. Do not label a sheath margin as the free ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COLLAR SEARCH VIEW ONLY — TRUE LIGULE UNMEASURED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FOLLOW THE ENTIRE NARROW PANICLE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Contracted, sometimes partly sheathed flowering head, about 1–5 cm long.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The 2023 revision describes a 1–5 cm × 0.1–0.4 cm interrupted, contracted panicle with mostly appressed branches about 0.2–1.2 cm long. Existing CC0 head photograph demonstrates actual attached spikelets along a narrow rachis, not a ruler-calibrated branch series. Photograph the entire flowering axis emerging from the upper sheath and include a centimeter ruler.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ATTACHED FLOWERING PHOTO — HEAD MEASUREMENTS FROM LITERATURE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · DISSECT A RIPE ONE-FLORET SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelet 1.4–2.4 mm; glumes 0.5–1.4 mm; lemma 1.3–2.4 mm, AWNLESS.
field_id_short_tiles.details: According to Peterson and colleagues (2023), each spikelet has one fertile floret. The two subequal usually one-veined glumes are 0.5–1.4 mm (occasionally 2–3 veins); the lanceolate fertile lemma is 1.3–2.4 mm, unawned, and the palea about 1–2 mm. Remove the glumes in order, then expose the lemma, palea and floret with 1-mm scale under 10–20×. Current whole-spikelet photos cannot prove separate bract measurements or veins; never draw arrows to unseen structures.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES + RELEASE GATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Separate aboveground-rooting nimblewill from underground-rhizomatous aparejo.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 8 is DIFFERENT-SPECIES M. schreberi for comparison only: its slender aboveground stolons can root at nodes, whereas M. utilis requires visible scaly underground rhizomes. Seep muhly (M. reverchonii) makes a tighter tuft and more open flowering panicle; pine muhly (M. dubia) is much larger, with a much longer ligule. Do not infer the held hybrid M. ×involuta from intermediate appearance. Remain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until all decisive anatomy and public QA are verified.
